sections.h2: Selling a house in Linden, NJ
sections.html:
Linden is a mix of industry and neighborhoods in Union County, roughly 13 miles southwest of Manhattan. A sale by agent, by owner or to a cash buyer ends the same way: a deed filed with the Union County Clerk in Elizabeth and the state transfer fee paid from the seller's side.

Population was 45,752 in mid-2025, 4.6% above the April 2020 base. The city covers 10.69 square miles of land, with another 0.73 square miles of water along the Arthur Kill, the channel that separates Linden from Staten Island. Owners live in 59.5% of homes, and a typical owner-held house is valued at $419,700.

More than half of residents speak a language besides English at home, so a closing attorney who can explain the documents in your own language is worth asking about.

Named areas inside the city include Bayway, Grasselli, Tremley, Wheatsheaf, Morses Mill, Vreeland Mills and Warners. Sunnyside is the residential section west of St. Georges Avenue, named for a former golf club, and it borders Clark, Cranford and Winfield on the west and Roselle on the east. Linden's eastern edge runs along the Arthur Kill and the Bayway Refinery, so a house in that part of town will draw questions about industrial neighbors that a western house will not.

The Raymond Wood Bauer Promenade hosts outdoor concerts in warm weather. About 85.7% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, so many neighbors are long-term owners and renters.

Transit shapes how buyers look at Linden houses, and the average commute is 31.5 minutes. The main options:

  • Rail: Linden station offers a one-seat ride to Manhattan in 39 minutes on the North Jersey Coast Line and Northeast Corridor Line.
  • Highways: the New Jersey Turnpike runs through the east side, Interstate 278 ends in Linden, and U.S. 1/9 and Route 27 cross the city. The Garden State Parkway runs about 500 feet beyond the western city line.
  • Bus: NJ Transit routes 112 and 115 run to Manhattan's Port Authority, and routes 48 and 94 serve Elizabeth and Newark.
  • Air: Newark Liberty is roughly a 15-minute drive, and Linden Airport takes small general aviation flights.

If your house is near the station, say so at the top of the listing or when you ask a cash buyer for an offer.

Linden Public Schools run prekindergarten through grade 12 and enrolled 6,125 students in 2022-23. Eight elementary schools (Schools 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10) cover PreK to grade 5, and McManus Middle School and Soehl Middle School cover grades 6 to 8. Families will ask which numbered school covers your block, so find out before you list.

sections.h2: What a Linden seller handles before closing
sections.html:
Call the City of Linden's construction and code office and ask which paperwork is due before closing: a continued certificate of occupancy, a fire inspection or a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. Ask about open permits on the property too, and request the answers in writing for the buyer's attorney. Resale rules differ from town to town in New Jersey, so do not assume a neighboring town's checklist applies.

Linden deeds go to the Union County Clerk at 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth, phone 908-527-4787. The recording office is open weekdays 8:30 to 4:30, takes over-the-counter filings until 3:30 and needs no appointment. Online land records cover June 1, 1977 onward, and a free property fraud alert program emails or calls subscribers when their name shows up on a recorded document. Signing up before you sell is a cheap precaution.

At a median value of $419,700, a typical Linden sale falls in the state's schedule for prices above $350,000, where the rate rises in steps with the price. Residential deeds above $1 million also carry a percentage fee. The seller bears both charges.

Buyers' attorneys usually ask for the same items, so collect them before you accept an offer.

  • Your latest tax bill and mortgage payoff statement.
  • The survey and any permit records for finished basements, additions or converted garages.
  • Leases and a rent roll if the house has tenants, which matters for two-family homes.
  • The city's written answer on certificates, so the buyer's side sees it early.

Once you sign a contract, the buyer's attorney or title agent orders a title search and asks the city for any certificate the house needs. If a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate or fire inspection is required, book it early, since the city sets its own scheduling and a missed slot can push the closing date. On closing day you sign the deed, the transfer fee and any tax payoff come out of your proceeds, and the title company sends the deed to the Union County Clerk for recording.

With a cash buyer, the lender's appraisal and underwriting drop out, so the city certificate is usually the longest remaining wait. Ask each buyer in writing who orders it and who pays for any repairs it calls for.

A two-family or rented house adds one more question: will the buyer keep the tenants or want the unit empty? Settle that before the contract, because it changes the price, the closing date and what you owe the tenants.

sections.h2: When a cash purchase suits a Linden house
sections.html:
A cash buyer is a good match when the house needs repairs, carries tenants or has to close on a firm date, because there are no loan conditions or repair demands to negotiate. A house in good condition may net more on the open market, where owner-occupants and investors compete.

Ask every buyer for written terms and compare them line by line, covering price, closing date, the transfer fee and responsibility for any city inspection. Two offers with the same headline number can leave you with different amounts at the table. Keep the survey, tax bills and permit paperwork in one folder, and ask your title company for a copy of your recorded deed after closing.

faqs.q: Will Linden's city office inspect my house before I sell?
faqs.a: Ask the City of Linden's construction and code office. Resale rules vary by town in New Jersey, so get written confirmation of any certificate your address needs and how long scheduling takes.

faqs.q: Who bears the transfer fee in a Linden sale?
faqs.a: The seller. It is calculated on the deed price and paid when the Union County Clerk records the deed. Sales over $1 million add a graduated percent fee, also on the seller.

faqs.q: Which office handles recording for Linden deeds?
faqs.a: The Union County Clerk's recording office, 2 Broad Street, Elizabeth. Recording takes no appointment.

faqs.q: Can a Linden rental or two-family house sell with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the buyer the leases and rent roll, and ask the city whether a rental registration or inspection is tied to the property. Get in writing whether each buyer will take the house with tenants in place.

faqs.q: How fast can a Linden house sale close?
faqs.a: Speed depends on who buys and on city paperwork. Without mortgage underwriting a cash deal can move sooner, but deed recording and any required city certificate still take their own time.
